topic: MRC NW-DMS; Yale PhD Public Health; Pittsburgh IBGP; Groningen Eric Bleumink Fellowship

items.official: Applications for 2027/28 entry are open until Friday, 27 November 2026.
items.note: No closing time of day stated on the page.

items.official: Programme page: 'a stipend at the UKRI rate for four years' (no figure). UKRI: minimum stipend 21,805 from 1 October 2026 (20,780 before).
items.note: Figure is the UKRI minimum, not printed on the Manchester page. Studentship starts Oct 2027 so the 2027/28 rate may be higher. Funding covers tuition 'at home or international rate'.

items.official: Studentships are available to UK and international applicants.
items.note: Fees funded at home or international rate.

items.claim: First or Upper Second (or international equivalent), no master's required
items.official: We expect applicants to hold, or be about to obtain, a First or Upper Second-class UK honours degree (or international equivalent) in a relevant discipline. ... many successful applicants may also have: A master's qualification.
items.note: Master's is not required but is listed as common among successful applicants. MBBS equivalence is not stated - ask fbmh.doctoralacademy.admissions@manchester.ac.uk.

items.claim: Up to two projects, each separate application
items.official: You can apply for up to two projects ... you must submit a separate application for each, including a supporting statement tailored to the specific project.
items.note: Contacting the supervisor first is described as 'one of the most important things you need to do before you apply'.

items.claim: Interviews w/c 8 Feb 2027; awards w/c 22 Feb 2027; start Oct 2027
items.official: Interviews take place: Week commencing 8 February 2027; Studentships awarded: Week commencing 22 February 2027; Studentship begins: October 2027
items.note: Projects and applications opened 30 Oct 2026. Interviews are on Teams, only for supervisor-nominated applicants; others are told they were unsuccessful. Interview includes a max 10-minute presentation.

items.official: Supporting statement; reference details; degree certificates and final/interim transcripts; official English certificates (if applicable); CV. 'A research statement is not required for this programme.'
items.note: Notes did not list CV as a requirement from the programme page - it is required. English test is NOT needed at application; only a condition of any offer.

items.official: we require two references from people who have knowledge of your academic ability ... one of these can be from your clinical or work background. Referee email must be institutional, not personal.
items.note: This is the FBMH general PGR page, not MRC-specific; MRC page says referees get an automatic request on submission and you cannot be nominated without references.

items.official: There is no specific word limit for your supporting statement, however, we would recommend two to four pages maximum.
items.note: Recommended 2-4 pages, not 1-2 (FBMH general page).

items.claim: English minimum not found; ask about waiver
items.official: Applicants are not required to meet the English language requirements at the point of application. ... any offer made will be conditional upon completion of an approved English language test (such as IELTS). FBMH general: typically IELTS 6.5 overall (5.5 each component, 6.0 writing) or TOEFL iBT 90; some programmes 7.0.
items.note: Tests valid 2 years; expiry before start requires a retake for CAS.

items.official: Not stated on the programme page or the pages read.
items.note: Confirm in portal.

items.official: Level: Postgraduate Research; Entry year 2027/28; Intake: September; Funding: Research Council / MRC PhD Studentship / Awarded / Fully Funded; main supervisor only.
items.note: Portal says Intake September although the studentship begins October 2027 - use these values exactly as the page instructs.

items.claim: Deadline 1 Dec 2026, 11:59 pm Eastern, GSAS not SOPHAS
items.official: Public Health listed under 'December 1, 2026'; 'All application deadlines are as of 11:59 pm Eastern time.' GSAS: public health PhD must use the GSAS PhD/Master's application.
items.note: Deadlines 'subject to change at any time'. Fall 2027 application is open at apply.grad.yale.edu/apply.

items.claim: Fee $105, waiver available incl. non-US citizens
items.official: The application fee for all degree-seeking applicants is US $105.00. US citizens, permanent residents, and non-US citizens are all eligible to request a fee waiver.

items.claim: 5-year funding guarantee for all YSPH PhD students
items.official: All PhD students are guaranteed five years of 12-month stipend and tuition support in the form of YSPH fellowships, teaching fellowships, traineeships and research assistantships. ... health award ... single-student Yale Health Plan Hospitalization/Specialty Coverage.
items.note: YSPH FAQ also adds spouse/family health coverage and a family subsidy for children under 18.

items.official: Tuition for full-time study at GSAS for 2026-2027 is $52,400. PhD fellowship covers full tuition through at least first five years.

items.claim: GSAS minimum stipend $52,046 (other band $53,629); Public Health band not found
items.official: 2026-27 minimum annual PhD stipends: Humanities/Social Sciences $52,046; Physical Sciences $52,046; Biological & Biomedical Sciences $53,629.
items.note: Public Health's band is not stated; $1,500 one-time relocation award in first payment confirmed on same page. Note stipend table rendered only via text fetch.

items.claim: GRE required only for Biostatistics and HPM; not accepted for the other four
items.official: GRE required for Biostatistics (PhD and MS), Health Policy Management (PhD). Not accepted for Chronic Disease Epidemiology, Environmental Health Sciences, Epidemiology of Microbial Diseases, Social and Behavioral Sciences (PhD).
items.note: YSPH: 'no minimum GRE'; 'Graduate School does not allow waivers'; GSAS: 'self-report scores and any future test dates'. Institution code 3987.

items.official: PhD section: 'minimum Speaking scores required to teach: TOEFL 26+ (before 21 Jan 2026) / 5.5+ (on or after); IELTS 8.0 or higher'. 100/7.0 is the stated minimum for the MS program only. Average admitted PhD: TOEFL 106, IELTS 7.5. 'We do not accept Duolingo.'
items.note: PhD page gives Speaking minimums (below them: possible August summer English programme), no overall minimum seen. 'IELTS 8.0 or higher' is as written (speaking). Accept only TOEFL iBT / IELTS Academic.

items.claim: Waiver: English-medium degree, >=3 years in residence
items.official: exempt ... if you received (or will receive) an undergraduate degree from a school where English is the primary language of instruction, and studied in residence for at least three years. No exemptions on basis of an advanced degree.
items.note: Self-declaration detail not seen on the pages read.

items.official: Three letters of recommendation. Recommenders enter names in the application and upload via link.
items.note: Letters need not arrive before submission, but programmes begin reviewing shortly after the deadline.

items.claim: Statement of Academic Purpose 500-1,000 words; up to 3 faculty
items.official: YSPH: applicants write about research interests and faculty; can list up to three faculty. YSPH page states no word limit. GSAS: prompt is in Application Question FAQs.
items.note: 500-1,000 word limit NOT found on pages read; faculty count and 'no mentor needed in advance' confirmed.

items.claim: No WES required; unofficial transcripts suffice
items.official: Unofficial transcripts should be uploaded with your application. Official or paper transcripts are not needed at this time. Records must be in English or translated.
items.note: Unofficial-transcript rule confirmed; no WES requirement seen anywhere, but no explicit 'no WES' statement found.

items.claim: No master's required; bachelor's or equivalent
items.official: A Master's degree is not required to apply for a PhD at Yale, although some programs give preference to applicants with post-baccalaureate training.
items.note: Applicable while degree in progress if completed before matriculation. MBBS equivalence not ruled on - email phdms.publichealth@yale.edu.

items.official: The 5-year-average acceptance is 3% across the 6 departments. Average GPA for admitted students: 3.8. There is no minimum GPA required.
items.note: Decisions mostly Feb-early March; reply by 15 April.

items.official: Resume/CV required; 'A writing sample is not required.'
The application fee is $50, which is due before we can begin processing your application.
items.note: Non-refundable; the notes say need-based waivers - not found on pages read.

items.official: The Fall 2027 application is open September 1 till December 1, 2026.
items.note: No time of day stated. FAQ: review is rolling and applying early is beneficial.

items.official: A minimum of three letters of recommendation.
items.note: Research-advisor letter 'very important' per FAQ.

items.official: Stipend: $41,200 for the 2026-2027 academic year; full tuition remission; individual health insurance; first-year educational enrichment $2,000.

minimum 100 iBT TOEFL (or 5 on new scoring), 7.0 IELTS, or 120 Duolingo. Scores less than 24 months old from September 1st of start term. Exempt if bachelor's or higher from a regionally accredited US or other approved English-instructed institution.
items.note: TOEFL institution code 2927, dept 45. 'Other approved English-instructed institution' is not defined on the page.

items.claim: Min GPA 3.2; incoming average 3.7; GRE not required
items.official: A minimum grade point average of 3.2 (on a scale of 4) or its equivalent. Average incoming GPA 3.7. GRE Scores are not required.
items.note: Degree must be 'in a biological or physical science or in mathematics, computer science or engineering' - an MBBS fit is for the program to judge. Research experience: all successful applicants have it, most 1+ year in a lab.

items.claim: Interviews Jan-Mar, offers by 15 April, overseas by teleconference
items.official: Most interviews take place between January through March. Applicants are accepted on a rolling basis between February 1 and April 15. All offer letters will be sent by mail before April 15. Overseas interviews may be by teleconference.
Apply Now link: https://learn.hs.pitt.edu/portal/gr_app. Personal statement required; research description 'heavily weighed'.
items.note: No word limit stated on pages read. CV not listed.

items.official: the Eric Bleumink Fellowship receives hundreds of applications each year and only four of them will be awarded with a scholarship.
items.note: 'Four' is from the Rules PDF (updated Nov 2024); 'worldwide' not stated.

items.claim: EUR 1,250/month living, EUR 275 settling, EUR 310/yr study allowance
items.official: A living allowance of EUR 1250,00 per month ... A settling allowance of EUR 275 ... A study allowance of EUR 310 per year for books and other study material. Tuition fees ... will be paid.
items.note: Plus train Schiphol-Groningen 2nd class. Public web page only says grant covers 'tuition fee, costs of international travel, subsistence, books, and health insurance'.

items.claim: Return flights Amsterdam to nearest home airport; insurance via AON; no clothing allowance
items.official: flights between Amsterdam and the airport nearest to the recipient's residence ... maximum fare economy ... AON ... A clothing allowance is not included.
items.note: Excess baggage not covered.

items.claim: No paid work, no family provision, must return home
items.official: may not enter into paid employment in the Netherlands; does not provide for the cost of bringing any members of the recipient's family; state that they will return to their own countries at the end.

items.claim: Nominees chosen first week of January; letter within a week; files before 1 Feb; fellows informed before 1 March
items.official: The Admission Office selects nominees in the first week of January; nominees send an EBF motivation letter within one week; files sent before the 1st of February; committee informs all nominees before 1st of March.
items.note: Web page says nominees are informed before 1 February; no contact by 1 Feb means not nominated. Admission offer needed before February.

items.official: It is not possible to actively apply for an Eric Bleumink Fellowship Talent Grant. Suitable candidates will be informed about a nomination.
items.note: msd@rug.nl is the Mobility and Scholarship Desk contact for Talent Grant questions (Rules PDF).

items.official: Appendix 1 (DAC ODA list, Least Developed Countries first preference) lists Bangladesh; the PDF table extracted as interleaved text, so tier column is inferred from order.
items.note: Bangladesh is on the country list; tier reading is from garbled layout - treat as likely, not certain. No Bangladeshi university appears in Appendix 2 (partner list): confirmed.

items.official: such a master application should be completed by the applicant before 1st of December.
items.note: Grant is for programmes starting September only; no other simultaneous Groningen scholarship allowed.

items.claim: Application fee EUR 100 non-Dutch diploma, once per academic year
items.official: The University of Groningen charges a non-refundable application fee of EUR 100 for applicants with a non-Dutch diploma. ... only need to pay the fee once per academic year.
items.note: Admissions Office cannot review until fee received.

items.official: Non-EU/EEA: 24900; EU/EEA: 2771

The entrance examination will be a test of your statistical knowledge. Passing the exam leads to an interview (online or in person), short presentation on a previous research project plus motivation; result in 2-3 weeks.
items.note: '1-hour' duration not seen on text fetch.

items.official: Groningen 2026/27 master's table groups IRHD (research) with IELTS Academic overall 6.5 (min 6.0 in all categories), TOEFL iBT 90 (min 21 each).
items.note: Search snippet shows min 6.0 per category in this table, not Speaking/Writing 6.5; the 2027/28 page lists IRHD under 'Level 2' with IELTS 6.5 overall, 6.0 L/R, 6.5 Speaking/Writing, TOEFL 90 - consistent with the notes. Not read in full.

items.claim: Programme deadline 1 May 2027 (irrelevant to Bleumink timeline)
items.official: IRHD programme page: 01 May 2027 for all. Groningen International Guide lists IRHD non-EU/EEA deadline as 1 March.
items.note: Conflict between programme page (1 May) and International Guide PDF (1 March non-EU). Use the programme page but verify.

items.claim: MBBS not named as qualifying degree
items.official: Page does not mention MBBS; Medicine is listed among admissible bachelor's degrees; Groningen Medicine bachelor graduates 'No additional requirements'. Other degrees assessed by the selection committee.
items.note: Ask irhd@umcg.nl (address not verified).

summary: Yale English minimum TOEFL 100/IELTS 7.0 is the MS rule; PhD page gives Speaking minimums only (avg admitted 106/7.5). Yale 500-1,000 word statement not found. MRC statement is 2-4 pages recommended, CV required, English needed only at offer, stipend figure is UKRI minimum (not on Manchester page), fee not found. Groningen IRHD deadline conflicts (1 May vs 1 March non-EU). Pittsburgh and EBF amounts all confirmed.
